title: Quarterly stabilization plan: proactive warm-pool scheduling & graceful autoscale
creator: Priya Patel
description: Goal: reduce tail latency and emergency prewarm runs by implementing a predictive warm-pool scheduler and a graded graceful-degradation path for Dedicated customers. This ticket captures the quarterly roadmap slice to design, validate, and pilot the scheduling heuristic plus the canary rollout and acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive scheduler deployed to canary region handling >= 25% of traffic for two strategic customers
Prewarm_hit_ratio improves by >= 30% on canary workloads vs baseline
90th-percentile queue_wait_ms reduced by at least 40% under representative surge tests
No more than 5% increase in token-cost-per-request compared to current baseline for canary customers
Runbook and rollback documented in Confluence with on-call playbook and SLAs
rollout_plan: Phase A (2 weeks): Lab validation using surge simulation harness; Phase B (weeks 3-4): Canary with two customers in us-west-2 on dedicated pools; Phase C (week 5): Expand to additional pools with gradual traffic shift and cost guardrails enabled. Immediate rollback: disable predictive scheduler and revert to baseline prewarm schedule. Post-mortem and metrics review at end of each phase.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Predictive model over-allocates and increases costs - Mitigation: conservative cost guardrail throttle and daily anomaly detection on cost_per_request_usd
Risk: New scheduler interacts poorly with autoscale burst lanes - Mitigation: coordinate with ENG autoscale feature toggle and add integration tests
Risk: Unexpected fallback model regressions - Mitigation: pin fallback to verified model profile and run evaluation suites against production prompt shards before canary
decisions: Use lightweight XGBoost time-series predictor for short-horizon demand (1-10m) to avoid heavy infra dependencies - agreed 2026-02-28
Keep KV-cache-enabled variants for prewarm paths; do not quantize prewarm-only model variants in this quarter - decision from ML review 2026-03-05
Throttle warm-pool growth with a soft cap of +20% of baseline during canary, adjustable by SRE on-call

2026-03-08: Design review feedback from Diego Morales: add canary customer opt-in consent flow and usage alerting in Console. Action: PM to create Console ticket.

2026-03-14: Budget review with Finance; approved burn window for canary with daily spend cap and automated pause on breach.
